summary: The stage-1 CUDA swap-AB MoE rewrite for T>32 targets the largest block in the problem: Marlin's 254/271 us (verify_16) and 443/427 us (verify_32) in profile a017e10aec544c55. Its floor and design hold up. One defect in the spec must be fixed before building. Each item must issue MMAs and ldmatrix only for ceil(routes_in_chunk/8) n8 fragments, not the full zero-filled 64 columns. Otherwise padded tensor work alone (~110 GFLOP at T=256) costs ~180 us and breaks M2.
justification: Mechanism. Under EP8 with ~4 (T=128) to ~8 (T=256) local routes per expert, the MoE GEMMs are a pure NVFP4 weight stream. With block_m capped at 16, Marlin re-streams an expert per m-block and runs at ~1.1 TB/s. Streaming each 128-row tile once per <=64-route chunk is the right fix. Numbers checked against profiles/submission.a017e10aec544c55.txt: Marlin is 254.0/270.7 us at verify_16 and 443.4/426.7 us at verify_32, act_and_mul is 5.8 us, and the moe_align kernel is ~3.6 us. FINDINGS.md quotes larger Marlin figures (284.9/466.8/501.0). The profile is the better source; judge milestones on profile rows from the same job type. Floor: muse_moe_w4a16 TASK.md gives 101.3/108.9 us at bs 128/256. The layer's own shape floors (126.6/143.8 us sliding, ~41 us of dense weights) leave ~100 us for the MoE, i.e. ~17 touched local experts (~490 MB). At 443 us that is ~1.1 TB/s, so the stated bandwidth is consistent. The design fits the hardware. A 4-stage ring of 16 KB codes, 2 KB scales and a 32 KB B slice is ~200 KB smem, which fits 1 CTA/SM on H100/H200, and 72 KB of weight bytes in flight per SM is enough for ~4.8 TB/s by Little's law. At T=256 there are ~1100 w13 items and ~550 w2 items over 132 SMs (~8 waves). The tail is about one item, ~288 KB, ~8 us at the per-SM bandwidth share. Dequant ALU is ~1-1.5 instructions per weight element: ~855M elements over 132 SMs, about 30-45 us, which overlaps the stream. The gate/up row interleave is correct for the m16n8k16 C fragment: c0,c1 sit at row lane/4 and c2,c3 at lane/4+8, so gate and up for the same intermediate column share a lane. Storing w*_gs only in the scale at dequant time keeps NVFP4 as NVFP4. Expected directions are consistent: the gate tokens>32 covers exactly verify_16/32 (T=128/256) and the T=33 and T=40 tests, and decode and verify_1 stay byte-identical. WEAKEST LINK: the spec says 'fp32 acc 16 x 64 per warp' and 'rows past the chunk zero-filled', which implies always computing 64 token columns. At T=256 that is ~1100+550 items x 128x4096x64x2 flop, about 110 GFLOP. mma.sync bf16 on Hopper reaches roughly 500-650 TFLOP/s, so that is ~170-220 us of tensor time, versus ~26 GFLOP of useful work. The MMA and ldmatrix loops must be bounded by a warp-uniform n8-fragment count from the work item (the route count is on device, so this is legal under graphs). The zero-filled B rows should also not be staged past that count. The B stage could be sized as 64 x 128 k so a 5th weight stage fits.
confounders: marlin-block-m-cap-16 (in master's lineage): it is the incumbent being replaced on exactly the gated shapes, so there is no interaction. Note that the incumbent figures are the capped-Marlin figures.
post-expert-norm-triton-small-t (in master): applies only at T<32. The gated shapes use the unchanged fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum, so no interaction.
sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (in master): changes routing numerics at T>=2, but identically for the incumbent and the candidate. The replaced-kernel comparison is unaffected.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite, judged on the replaced kernels' own rows (moe_route_list + moe_w13_silu_swapab + moe_w2_swapab vs 2x Marlin + act_and_mul + align) at verify_16/32. Nothing landed touches T>32 MoE except the cap-16 incumbent, which is fully replaced. The ungated shapes (decode_*, verify_1) are built-in controls because they keep master's code path. An ab-revert or control would not make the result easier to read; the next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: load_inline spawns nvcc in prepare(). The rules reject submissions that 'start processes'. muse_attention_decode/submission.py already uses load_inline, and the brief says it compiled in 41 s in a passing run. Confirm that run passed the static check (not just a check run that errored later) before relying on it.

Keep compile + Marlin bank + RoPE table + self-check inside prepare's 300 s and the 15 min run. Keep the NVFP4 bank in its packed form: re-tiling codes and e4m3 scales is lossless and allowed, but no bf16 copy of the weights may be stored.

kernel_fn must not branch on route counts on the host. The spec puts counts, work lists and the counter resets on device in route_list with a fixed grid, which is correct. Allocate act and y by shape only (T*8 rows), or preallocate in state per T.
Remote y rows stay uninitialised, as with Marlin today. The NaN-prefill self-check covers the combine's reliance on slot_expert_ids. Keep that check.
open_questions: Does the implementation bound the MMA/ldmatrix loops per item by ceil(routes/8) n8 fragments? Without this, M2 is unreachable (see the weakest link).
Is act indexed by t*8+s (like Marlin's cache2) or by position in route_idx? Kernels 2 and 3 must agree, and the w2 B gather depends on which. route_idx order makes w2's B rows contiguous per expert.

In the w13 epilogue each lane holds one intermediate column for two tokens, so stores to act are 2-byte scattered writes. Stage through smem for 16-byte row stores. The total is only ~2 MB, so this is low priority.

Under 'dist soft', how many distinct local experts are touched at T=128/256? If it is closer to 25-32 than ~17, the true MoE floor is ~150-190 us, and M2 (<=200 us at T=256) needs >4 TB/s rather than 2.6.

Rounding the e4m3*gs product to bf16 and multiplying by e2m1 in bf16x2 adds up to ~2^-9 relative error per element versus Marlin. That is expected to fit the 1e-2 per-row bound; confirm with the self-check's max row rel.
